Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
331 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Gale Warnings have been dropped. Only one Coastal Flood Warning
remaining at this time for Anne Arundel County. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Minor coastal flooding persists while winds continue to
    diminish. Light mountain snow showers expected in the
    Alleghenies. 

- 2) Another potent area of low pressure brings precipitation
     and blustery conditions Sunday night into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Minor coastal flooding persists while winds continue to
diminish. Light mountain snow showers expected in the 
Alleghenies. 

Low pressure along the St. Lawrence River Valley will continue
to move farther away from the local area tonight, moving into
the Canadian Maritimes Saturday. Pressure gradient will continue
to relax tonight into Saturday with a continued gradually
downward trend in winds expected, although it will still be
breezy tomorrow. Some breaks in the cloud cover are possible
tonight, but it will still remain mostly cloudy or cloudy at
times. Mountain snow showers are possible, but the saturation
layer will get shallower tonight resulting in loss of ice
crystals and poor SLRs. Winter Weather Advisories were kept
because of the threat of light icing, since snow accumulations
aren't likely to meet the criteria for Winter Wx Advisory.

Still breezy tomorrow, but with ample sunshine as shortwave
ridging starts building in. Winds decouple Sat night as surface
ridging builds in. Cold Saturday night with lows in the 30s.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Another potent area of low pressure brings precipitation
and blustery conditions Sunday night into Monday.

High pressure will keep the region dry Sunday. Temperatures will be 
near seasonable with highs middle 50s to lower 60s. 

As the high pushes further to the southeast Sunday night, a low 
pressure system will move from the middle Mississippi Valley on 
Sunday toward the eastern Great Lakes Sunday night. A trailing cold 
front will push across the region Sunday night into Monday morning.
Showers will likely accompany the front. We can't rule out a clap of 
thunder or two either given that there will be plenty of wind shear, 
despite instability being minimal to nil and the time of night for 
frontal passage. Highs cooler Sunday with highs mainly in lower to 
upper 50s.

As the front pushes through, winds will pick up substantially out of 
the northwest on Monday in its wake. Wind gusts, especially along 
the ridges out west, could approach wind advisory criteria. Areas 
along the MD/PA border will also see gusts close to criteria, but 
not very high confidence in the exact magnitude at this time. Still, 
potential for downed trees given the wet ground from the previous 
system. Otherwise, highs Monday reach the upper 40s to mid 50s 
outside of the mountains (they'll be in the 20s to 30s). Wind chills 
will be quite cold on the ridges Monday, with values in the teens at 
the highest elevations. 

Once the front moves to the east and southeast Monday afternoon, 
high pressure will become reestablished and bring dry conditions and 
seasonable temperatures to the region through the middle of the 
week. 

&&

.AVIATION /19Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...

Winds will lose some of its gustiness tonight, but remain around
10 kt. Winds pick up again Saturday with daytime mixing with
gusts to around 22 kt expected. Winds become lighter on Sunday
as high pressure builds traverses the area, but turn from a
southerly direction. Showers are expected Sunday night.

Winds out of the WNW Monday afternoon at around 15 to 25 knots, 
gusting up to 35 to 40 knots at times in the wake of a powerful cold 
front. Flight category should return to VFR by Monday morning and 
remain that way through at least the middle of the week. 

&&

.MARINE...

All Gale Warnings have been dropped as winds continue to
diminish. However, SCA conditions will continue through
Saturday with gusts up to 25 kt expected. 

An area of low pressure will slide by to our northwest Sunday into 
Monday. Gale-force winds are possible Monday in the wake of the cold 
front associated with this system. Winds will rapidly taper off 
Monday night into Tuesday, with any marine headlines likely dropping 
overnight Monday. Light and variable winds prevail Tuesday and 
Wednesday. 

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...

Tidal anomalies have dropped at least one to two feet since
yesterday, but lingering coastal flooding issues remain at many
of our tidal locations. Expect another high tide cycle of minor
coastal flooding at the most sensitive locations like Annapolis.

&&

.CLIMATE...

weather stations. Note, this is for Thanksgiving Day, which is
separate from the daily records for November 26.
